result.title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model
result.summary: AI research agents can propose, execute, and improve programs that solve machine learning tasks. However, executing each candidate program requires training and evaluating ML models, limiting how many candidates an agent can explore at each step. We introduce MLE-World, a world model finetuned from Qwen3.5-4B that predicts a program's terminal output (error traces, training logs, and validation scores) from its code and data description without executing it, together with a confidence score estimating the prediction's correctness. Because a prediction costs one inference call rather than a training run, MLE-World makes test time scaling (TTS) affordable for these agents. We build five TTS policies, guided by MLE-World, that compare several candidates per step by their predicted outputs: Sequential revision, Best-of-N, Pairwise judging, Fusion, and a UCB style rule that also adds an exploration bonus from this confidence score. Since predictions can be wrong, we run a candidate for real only when its confidence score is low. On 17 MLE-bench Lite tasks, MLE-World matches the real terminal output on 77.9% of held out programs, versus 41.1% for much larger prompted models. MLE-World guided TTS achieves up to 22.1% higher observed mean performance than the agent without a world model, with less real execution. Project webpage: https://mle-world.github.io/.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文微调 Qwen3.5-4B 构建世界模型 MLE-World，从代码与数据描述直接预测 ML 程序的最终输出（报错、训练日志、验证分数）并给出置信度，再据此设计多种 test-time scaling 策略来选择候选程序。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测执行结果＋置信度决定是否真实执行」可类比 LVR 中廉价预测状态与按不确定性触发的 LOOK/STOP 决策，可能为视觉证据获取与停止准则提供借鉴。
